C45038.observed: What was checked: that choosing a part from the catalogue fills in the cost and the selling price by itself, and shows them as money. What happened: typing "King" into the Part number box brought up a list of catalogue parts. Choosing one filled the Description in automatically, put 35.12 into Cost and 62.71 into Sell price without any typing, and both boxes carry a $ sign in front of the figure.

C45051.observed: What was checked: that pressing the Escape key closes the quick row, the same as it does in Tech View. What happened: on an empty row, Escape closed it straight away with no questions asked. On a row with something typed into it, Escape brought up the "Discard this part?" warning first with "Keep Editing" ready to press - so your typing cannot vanish by accident - and choosing "Discard Part" then closed the row. That is the correct behaviour for both cases. The close (×) button was checked alongside and behaves identically.

C45052.observed: What was checked: that clicking somewhere else on the page does not throw away a part you are part-way through typing. What happened: with "ZZAUTOTEST validation2" typed into the row, clicking well away from it on the page left the row open and the text still in it. Nothing was lost and nothing closed.

C45053.observed: What was checked: that the little keyboard-shortcut reminder under the row includes the Shift+Enter shortcut for Full View users, and that Tech View users do not get that extra line. What happened: in Full View the reminder shows the Enter, Tab and Esc shortcuts and also the Shift+Enter "more options" shortcut. Checked in Tech View earlier on the same build, the reminder showed only Enter, Tab and Esc - no Shift+Enter. So the extra line appears only where it should.

C45056.observed: What was checked: that when several required boxes are empty, one single message tells you all of them - including the cost and the selling price. What happened: filling in only a description and pressing Save produced one message reading "Enter a qty, cost and sell price to save this part." It names all three missing items together rather than making you find them one at a time, and it names cost and sell price as the test requires. The row stayed open with the typing intact.
